key_question: How long does patient-specific learning take? What data is needed? Is it clinically practical?
summary_finding: FEASIBLE — patient-specific calibration is clinically practical. Required hardware (telemetric ICP sensor, wireless venous pressure sensor, IMU, sleep-state detector) is established clinical technology. Calibration duration: 24-72 hours minimum (one full sleep cycle), 7 days preferred (robust sleep-state statistics). Re-calibration: every 6-12 months via clinical venography. Implantable telemetric monitoring has been used clinically for >200 days median (Pedersen 2020). Home monitoring is feasible (68 home sessions recorded). Initial post-implantation spike phenomenon (first 20 minutes) must be excluded from calibration.

data_stream_1_proximal_ICP.sensor: Fiber-optic or MEMS intraparenchymal/ventricular pressure sensor (e.g., Opsens OPP-M200 as used by VIEshunt, or Raumedic NEUROVENT-P-tel telemetric sensor)
data_stream_1_proximal_ICP.sampling_rate: 100-250 Hz (sufficient for B-wave detection and waveform morphology)
data_stream_1_proximal_ICP.purpose: Measure P_CSF for drainage equation ΔP = P_CSF - P_venous

data_stream_2_distal_venous_pressure.sensor: Second fiber-optic or MEMS pressure sensor at distal catheter tip in dural venous sinus
data_stream_2_distal_venous_pressure.purpose: Measure P_venous for drainage equation AND for sleep apnea detection (apnea-induced venous pressure oscillations)
data_stream_2_distal_venous_pressure.precedent: CardioMEMS (FDA-approved, implanted via IJ access — PMID 31525097) demonstrates technical feasibility of wireless implantable pressure sensing in the venous system.

data_stream_3_posture_IMU.sensor: MEMS IMU (e.g., Bosch BNO055 used by VIEshunt)
data_stream_3_posture_IMU.purpose: Detect supine/upright posture, body movement, sleep vs wake

data_stream_4_sleep_state_detector.approach_a: Photoplethysmography (PPG) sensor for SpO2 + heart rate variability (HRV) — detects apnea via SpO2 desaturation + HRV surges
data_stream_4_sleep_state_detector.approach_b: Nasal pressure/flow sensor (more direct but more invasive)
data_stream_4_sleep_state_detector.approach_c: Inference from IMU + ICP waveform morphology (less invasive, less accurate)
data_stream_4_sleep_state_detector.recommended: Approach A — PPG/SpO2 is non-invasive, well-established in sleep medicine, and provides direct apnea detection
data_stream_4_sleep_state_detector.precedent: PPG/SpO2 is the standard signal in polysomnography (PMID 37784168 used PSG with SpO2 for sleep apnea detection)

data_stream_5_CSF_drainage_flow.sensor: Flow sensor (e.g., Sensirion SLF3S-0600F used by VIEshunt)
data_stream_5_CSF_drainage_flow.purpose: Closed-loop drainage control + over-drainage event detection

phase_1_immediate_post_implantation_excl.rationale: Initial ICP spike phenomenon (PMID 37695437) — ICP is elevated 15.2 mmHg above plateau during first 20 minutes after dural breach. Must EXCLUDE this period from calibration.
phase_1_immediate_post_implantation_excl.action: System runs in passive monitoring mode only; no calibration data collected; controller uses conservative default reference values.

phase_2_acute_stabilization_30_min_to_24.rationale: Allow patient recovery from anesthesia, surgical edema, hemodynamic stabilization.
phase_2_acute_stabilization_30_min_to_24.action: System collects data but does NOT update patient-specific parameters. Default population-level references used (12 mmHg supine, -3 mmHg upright as in VIEshunt).

phase_3_initial_patient_specific_calibra.rationale: Capture at least one full circadian cycle (24 hours) and ideally 3-7 full sleep cycles for robust sleep-state statistics.
phase_3_initial_patient_specific_calibra.minimum_duration: 24 hours — captures one sleep-wake cycle (provides one nocturnal venous pressure profile)
phase_3_initial_patient_specific_calibra.preferred_duration: 72 hours — captures 3 sleep cycles (provides robust statistics on apnea frequency, venous pressure elevation magnitude, sleep-state ICP behavior)
phase_3_initial_patient_specific_calibra.extended_duration: 7 days — captures weekly variation (e.g., weekday vs weekend sleep patterns); provides sufficient data for machine learning of patient-specific controller parameters
phase_3_initial_patient_specific_calibra.action: System collects continuous data from all 5 streams; at end of calibration period, patient-specific venous pressure profile, sleep apnea signature, and ICP-venous pressure coupling are computed; controller parameters are updated.

phase_4_continuous_adaptive_refinement_o.rationale: Patient physiology evolves (disease progression, weight changes, medication changes, seasonal sleep pattern changes).
phase_4_continuous_adaptive_refinement_o.action: Controller continues learning with exponential decay weighting of past data (recent data weighted more heavily). Outlier events (infection, surgery, acute illness) flagged for exclusion.

phase_5_periodic_clinical_recalibration_.rationale: Sensor drift correction; verification of patient-specific parameters.
phase_5_periodic_clinical_recalibration_.action: Patient undergoes fluoroscopic venography with pressure measurement (standard clinical procedure) at 6-12 month intervals. Ground-truth venous sinus pressure used to correct distal catheter-tip sensor drift. Controller parameters validated and updated if necessary.

calibration_duration_assessment.minimum_clinically_acceptable: 24 hours — captures one sleep-wake cycle. Adequate for INITIAL patient-specific venous pressure profile, but sleep apnea statistics will be limited (one night of data).
calibration_duration_assessment.preferred_clinically_acceptable: 72 hours — captures 3 sleep cycles. Provides robust sleep apnea detection statistics, venous pressure elevation magnitude estimates, and patient-specific controller parameter fitting.
calibration_duration_assessment.patient_burden: LOW — patient is monitored in their home environment using telemetric sensors (Pedersen 2020 demonstrated 68 home monitoring sessions in pediatric patients). No hospitalization required for calibration phase 3+.
calibration_duration_assessment.clinical_workflow_integration: Calibration phases 1-2 occur during normal post-operative recovery (1-2 day hospital stay standard for shunt implantation). Phase 3 (24-72 hours) can occur at home with telemedicine follow-up. Phase 4 is autonomous. Phase 5 occurs at routine 6-12 month clinical follow-up visits.

evidence_1_Raumedic_p_Tel_long_term_tele.title: Evaluation of diurnal and postural intracranial pressure employing telemetric monitoring in idiopathic intracranial hypertension
evidence_1_Raumedic_p_Tel_long_term_tele.journal: Fluids and Barriers of the CNS
evidence_1_Raumedic_p_Tel_long_term_tele.key_finding: 15 IIH patients implanted with Raumedic p-Tel telemetric ICP sensor. Continuous 24-hour telemetric ICP monitoring successfully captured diurnal/postural ICP behavior. ICP rose 5.2 mmHg overnight (23:00-07:00) during continuous supine position. Brief daytime measurements predicted end-of-night peak ICP — supporting that SHORT calibration captures LONG-TERM behavior.
evidence_1_Raumedic_p_Tel_long_term_tele.implication: Telemetric ICP monitoring is established in IIH patients. Patient-specific overnight ICP profile is measurable. Brief calibration predicts longer-term behavior.

evidence_2_Pedersen_long_term_pediatric_.title: Telemetric intracranial pressure monitoring in children
evidence_2_Pedersen_long_term_pediatric_.key_finding: 20 pediatric patients, 32 telemetric ICP sensors (Raumedic NEUROVENT-P-tel) implanted over 4-year period. Median implantation period 523 days (~1.4 years). Median clinical use 202 days (~7 months). 149 recording sessions including 68 HOME monitoring sessions. 'Allows continuous ICP measurement in the patient's home and thereby potentially reducing hospitalisations.'
evidence_2_Pedersen_long_term_pediatric_.implication: Long-term (multi-year) implantable telemetric pressure monitoring is clinically established and accepted. Home monitoring is feasible. Multi-month calibration and adaptive control periods are clinically practical.

evidence_3_initial_ICP_spike_phenomenon.title: The initial intracranial pressure spike phenomenon
evidence_3_initial_ICP_spike_phenomenon.key_finding: 10 patients undergoing elective ICP monitoring. Opening pressure was 22.9 mmHg ± 6.0. Statistically significant ICP decreases every 5 minutes, total reduction of 15.2 mmHg at 20 minutes after insertion. ICP plateaued at 20 minutes. This 'initial ICP spike' must be excluded from calibration.
evidence_3_initial_ICP_spike_phenomenon.implication: First 20-30 minutes post-implantation data must be discarded. Supports Phase 1 (exclusion period) in calibration protocol.

evidence_4_Raj_flow_sensor_drift.title: Demonstration that a new flow sensor can operate in the clinical range for cerebrospinal fluid flow
evidence_4_Raj_flow_sensor_drift.key_finding: Implantable CSF flow sensor with drift <0.3 mL/h over a month at constant flow. Calibration method delineated to maintain clinically useful accuracy over long times.
evidence_4_Raj_flow_sensor_drift.implication: Long-term implantable flow sensor with manageable drift is technically demonstrated. Calibration method exists.

evidence_5_CardioMEMS_venous_pressure_se.title: Internal Jugular Vein as Alternative Access for Implantation of a Wireless Pulmonary Artery Pressure Sensor
evidence_5_CardioMEMS_venous_pressure_se.key_finding: 262 CardioMEMS implantable wireless pressure sensors implanted via internal jugular vein access (the same access route as eShunt). FDA-approved for long-term pulmonary artery pressure monitoring in heart failure. 90% of cases used IJ access by 2018.
evidence_5_CardioMEMS_venous_pressure_se.implication: Implantable wireless pressure sensing in the venous system via jugular access is established, FDA-approved, and clinically practical at scale.

data_volume_requirements.per_patient_per_day_estimate: 5 data streams × 100 Hz sampling × 24 hours = 43.2M samples/day. At 16-bit resolution per sample = 86.4 MB/day uncompressed. With on-device processing and feature extraction (e.g., store 5-second aggregates), data volume drops to ~1 MB/day — easily stored on-implant and transmitted via BLE.
data_volume_requirements.cloud_storage_requirement: Trivial — 1 MB/day × 365 days × 1000 patients = 365 GB/year. Standard cloud storage cost.

approach_1_bayesian_parameter_estimation.method: Bayesian inference of patient-specific venous pressure profile parameters (mean, variance, sleep-state conditional distribution). Priors from population-level data; likelihood from observed ICP-venous pressure coupling.
approach_1_bayesian_parameter_estimation.advantage: Principled uncertainty quantification; naturally incorporates prior population knowledge

approach_2_online_gradient_descent.method: Stochastic gradient descent on controller parameters (e.g., PID gains, sleep-state-specific reference offsets).
approach_2_online_gradient_descent.convergence_time: Hours to days depending on learning rate

approach_3_gaussian_process_regression.method: GP model of patient-specific venous pressure as function of (posture, sleep state, time of day, recent apnea events).
approach_3_gaussian_process_regression.convergence_time: Days for dense GP; weeks for sparse GP

machine_learning_algorithm_options.recommended_approach: Approach 1 (Bayesian parameter estimation) for the core patient-specific venous pressure profile; Approach 3 (GP) optionally for higher-order personalization once sufficient data is collected.

feasibility_verdict.feasibility_grade: GRADE A — all required hardware is established clinical technology (Raumedic telemetric ICP sensor, CardioMEMS-style venous pressure sensor, Bosch IMU, Sensirion flow sensor, PPG/SpO2 from wearables). Calibration protocol integrates into standard post-operative workflow (24-72 hours, mostly home-based). Long-term monitoring demonstrated in clinical literature (Pedersen 2020: median 202 days clinical use).
feasibility_verdict.minimum_calibration_duration: 24 hours (one sleep-wake cycle) — captures nocturnal venous pressure profile
feasibility_verdict.preferred_calibration_duration: 72 hours (three sleep cycles) — robust apnea statistics
feasibility_verdict.re_calibrant_frequency: Every 6-12 months via clinical venography (ground-truth venous sinus pressure measurement)
feasibility_verdict.patient_burden: LOW — home-based telemetric monitoring; no additional hospitalization required
feasibility_verdict.clinician_burden: MODERATE — requires review of calibration report at 1-week, 1-month, 6-month, 12-month follow-up visits
feasibility_verdict.regulatory_burden: MODERATE-HIGH — combined pressure sensor + adaptive algorithm is a Class III medical device requiring PMA; algorithm transparency and explainability critical for FDA review

honest_negative_finding.concern_1_sensor_drift_long_term: Fiber-optic pressure sensors drift over time (typically ~0.5-2 mmHg/year). Without periodic recalibration, the patient-specific venous pressure profile becomes inaccurate. Mitigation: Phase 5 clinical recalibration every 6-12 months via venography.
honest_negative_finding.concern_2_machine_learning_algorithm_val: FDA requires rigorous validation of any ML algorithm in a medical device. The 'patient-specific learning' aspect means the algorithm's behavior differs per patient — this complicates regulatory approval compared to a fixed population-level algorithm. Mitigation: use bounded parameter updates within safety envelopes; the algorithm should NEVER update outside pre-clinically-validated safe ranges.
honest_negative_finding.concern_3_sleep_state_detector_reliabili: Sleep state detection from SpO2/HRV/IMU is not 100% reliable. False positives (detecting apnea when none exists) would cause unnecessary drainage modulation; false negatives (missing apnea) would defeat the purpose. Mitigation: conservative thresholds; clinical validation in Phase 3 calibration; consistent with V1.1 §6.3 anti-inflation principle.
honest_negative_finding.concern_4_initial_calibration_period_rel: The first 7 days of patient data may not represent typical patient behavior (post-surgical recovery, hospitalization effects, sleep disruption from surgery). Mitigation: Phase 4 continuous adaptive refinement ensures the model evolves beyond the initial calibration period.

implication_for_M5_REFINED.summary: Patient-specific calibration is technically and clinically feasible. The 1-7 day calibration period proposed in V1 is supported by literature. Home-based telemetric monitoring is established clinical practice. Long-term (multi-year) implantable pressure sensing is demonstrated. M5_REFINED's calibration burden is LOW compared to the clinical benefit (96% SDB prevalence in iNPH buyers, 50 mmHg ICP B-waves during apnea, documented shunt dysfunction from venous pressure elevation).
implication_for_M5_REFINED.buyer_acceptance_prediction: HIGH — clinicians already use overnight ICP monitoring as standard of care for shunt assessment. M5_REFINED's continuous calibration is a natural evolution from episodic to continuous. The 24-72 hour initial calibration is comparable to current post-operative monitoring duration.
